title: Review: Superposition, interference and coherence; Young's double slit; Stationary waves and harmonics
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W06-uk1#t2 term and clue written for the game; W06-uk1#t1 term and clue written for the game; W07-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; W07-uk1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: W06-uk1#N.10, W07-1#N.2, W10-1#N.4a, W10-uk1#N.6, W07-1#N.9a, W10-1#N.8a, W10-uk1#N.10, W07-1#N.6a, W10-uk1#N.8. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Antiphase
items.clue: Relation between two sources that adds π everywhere, turning every maximum into a minimum.

items.label: Phase difference
items.clue: How far one oscillation is ahead of another, as a fraction of a cycle expressed in radians.

items.label: Fringe spacing
items.clue: Distance between adjacent bright bands: λ times screen distance divided by slit separation.

items.label: Single slit
items.clue: Narrow opening placed after a lamp and filter so that both later openings are lit from one point.

questions.stem: Two loudspeakers, driven in phase by the same signal generator, face a line along which a microphone is moved. Starting from the central maximum of loudness, the microphone is moved along the line to the third maximum away from the centre. At that point its distances from the two speakers differ by 0.60 m. What is the wavelength of the sound?
Predict first. Monochromatic light passes through two very narrow slits and falls on a distant screen, producing a pattern of bright and dark bands. Which explanation accounts for this pattern?

options.text: Light travels straight through the slits, and each bright band is an image of a slit.
Light spreads out from each slit, and the waves from the two slits overlap and interfere.
Light is refracted at the edges of each slit, which bends it into separate bright bands.
Waves from the two slits interfere where they meet, so no spreading at the slits is needed.

questions.stem: A string fixed at both ends vibrates in a standing wave. Its nodes are at x = 0, 0.40 m, 0.80 m and 1.20 m, measured from one end. Points P, Q and R on the string are at x = 0.10 m, 0.20 m and 0.70 m. Which statement about the oscillations of P, Q and R is correct?

options.text: P and Q oscillate π/4 rad out of phase, being λ/8 apart.
P and Q oscillate in phase, with amplitudes equal to each other.
P and R oscillate in antiphase, with equal amplitudes.
P and R oscillate in phase, with equal amplitudes.

questions.stem: A tuning fork of frequency 384 Hz is held over a resonance tube. The first resonance occurs when the air column is 22.0 cm long. Ignoring any end correction, what is the speed of sound in the air?
questions.explanation: First resonance: L = λ/4, so λ = 4 × 0.220 = 0.880 m. v = fλ = 384 × 0.880 = 338 m s⁻¹.

questions.stem: Laser light passes through two slits 0.25 mm apart onto a wall 2.50 m away. A student measures across six fringe spacings: the fringes span 39.0 mm. What is the wavelength of the light?
questions.explanation: Fringe spacing = 39.0 mm ÷ 6 = 6.5 mm. λ = slit separation × fringe spacing ÷ slits-to-screen distance = (0.25 × 10⁻³ × 6.5 × 10⁻³)/2.50 = 6.5 × 10⁻⁷ m: red light.

questions.stem: A pipe of length 0.68 m is closed at one end and open at the other. The speed of sound in the air in the pipe is 340 m s⁻¹. Which gives, in increasing order, the lowest frequencies at which the air in the pipe resonates?
A loudspeaker emitting a 1000 Hz note faces a hard wall. A microphone moved along the line between them detects positions of minimum loudness 0.17 m apart. What is the speed of sound?
questions.explanation: Node to node = λ/2, so λ = 0.34 m. v = fλ = 1000 × 0.34 = 340 m s⁻¹.

questions.stem: In a Young's double-slit experiment, monochromatic red light is incident normally on the slits and the fringe separation on the screen is 2.0 mm. Which single change would make the fringe separation 4.0 mm?

options.text: Doubling the distance between the centres of the slits
Using blue light, of shorter wavelength, in place of the red
Halving the width of each slit, keeping their separation
Halving the distance between the centres of the two slits

questions.stem: A probe is moved between a microwave transmitter and a metal reflector. Adjacent minima of the received signal are 1.5 cm apart. What is the frequency of the microwaves?
questions.explanation: Node to node = λ/2, so λ = 3.0 cm. f = c/λ = 3.00 × 10⁸ ÷ 0.030 = 1.0 × 10¹⁰ Hz.
